verified.customer_question: I have £32,000 gross rent in 2025/26 and £45,000 PAYE salary. Do I start MTD in April 2027?
verified.live_or_handler_answer:
Yes — if your qualifying income was more than £30,000 for 2025-26, you need to use Making Tax Digital for Income Tax from 6 April 2027. Qualifying income means self-employment and property income before expenses (turnover/gross), not profit. Property and self-employment income is also usually reported through Self Assessment — MTD does not replace that annual return. Your PAYE/employment salary is not included in qualifying income for MTD for Income Tax.

Official guidance: https://www.gov.uk/guidance/find-out-if-and-when-you-need-to-use-making-tax-digital-for-income-tax

verified.customer_question: I made £70,000 profit but £90,000 turnover in 2024/25. Which number matters?
verified.live_or_handler_answer:
For Making Tax Digital for Income Tax, qualifying income uses turnover/gross from self-employment and property before expenses — not profit after expenses. So the turnover figure is the one that matters for the MTD threshold test (Self Assessment taxable profit is a different question). Using turnover of £90,000 for 2024-25, that is more than £50,000, so Making Tax Digital for Income Tax would usually start from 6 April 2026 (if you are a sole trader/landlord in Self Assessment). VAT is a separate regime with its own rolling 12-month taxable-turnover rules — do not treat the MTD test as the VAT test.

Official guidance: https://www.gov.uk/guidance/work-out-your-qualifying-income-for-making-tax-digital-for-income-tax

verified.customer_question: What is the difference between repairs and improvements for landlords?
verified.live_or_handler_answer: For property rental income, allowable expenses usually include maintenance and repairs that restore the property toward its original condition (for example fixing a leak, replacing a broken boiler, or redecorating between tenants). Improvements and other capital expenditure — work that adds something new, or alters/upgrades the property (for example an extension or a higher-specification kitchen) — are generally not deductible against rental income (keep records; they may matter for Capital Gains Tax later). Borderline cases can be fact-specific; use GOV.UK and consider an accountant for unusual works. https://www.gov.uk/guidance/income-tax-when-you-rent-out-a-property-working-out-your-rental-income
